messages:
Maria B: FYI — product is going to flip a new 'Pro Plus' packaging tomorrow morning, marketing expects higher quota per account. Need short capacity forecast for GPUs and potential mitigations.

Devon C: Can we get a conservative/likely/upside sims? I put together a quick baseline but missing region split. :thinking:

Ian W: Conservative = +30% requests to hosted API per seat -> roughly +22 GPU-hours/day in us-west with our current batching. Likely = +75% -> 55 GPU-hrs/day. Upside = x2 -> 120 GPU-hrs/day. These assume average seq_len 512 and 50% cache hit.

Ashley S: Tagging finance-bot for cost delta. Also note APAC capacity limited; if traffic shifts we might saturate sydney pools.

finance-bot: Estimated cost impact (monthly): conservative = $18k, likely = $45k, upside = $98k. Excludes Dedicated reserve discounts.

Devon C: Ran quick sim (local):
```
python sims/surge.py --cohort proplus --conv-rate 0.03 --seq 512 --regions us-west,us-east,eu
```
Devon C: Outputs: peak qps 3100, 95p latency drift +120ms if not throttled. Prefetch/batching salvage ~28% token cost.

Maria B: Options we should consider: 1) temporary rate-limits for new tier on hosted API 2) push canary to Dedicated for top customers 3) spike autoscale policy change 4) pre-buy 100 GPU-hrs in us-west for next 14 days.

Ian W: My preference: short-term rate cap + notify SRE to pre-warm nodes in us-west + run canary with 10 customers on Dedicated. If conversion meets likely, we should request procurement for additional reserved nodes.

Ashley S: APAC constraint — we should also schedule a cross-region failover doc. If sydney is tight, route to tokyo or us-west with notice to customers.

sre-bot: Alert created: #prewarm-us-west, runbook stub gen at /incidents/prewarm-us-west. Assigned to Ian W and Devon C.

Maria B: Great. @Devon_C can you produce a 24-hr rolling sim and a one-week cost bake by EOD? I'll sync with growth for rollout throttles.

Devon C: On it — will post sims link in this thread before 5pm. :thumbsup:
